text: Close to grabbing a franchise record all for himself, Kawhi Leonard elected to take a pass so he could be fresh for another day. Team-oriented to the core, Leonard was actually a bit selfish by request Sunday, scoring a career-high 55 points to lift the LA Clippers to a 112-99 victory over the Eastern Conference-leading Detroit Pistons. The Clippers are now on a season-best four-game winning streak and a recent scoring burst from Leonard is the primary reason. Leonard was told by head coach Tyronn Lue he was closing in on the franchise scoring record but decided to keep his fourth-quarter court time to a modest six minutes and departed with just under a minute remaining.He now shares the team mark for points in a game with teammate James Harden. "Like I told [Lue], I would rather play another game than go out there and risk it," Leonard said. "Hopefully, we can get another win and be in the same situation. It is what it is."ESPN
